description: tests/integration/mcp/test_durable_jobs.py:444 sets lease_seconds=0.05, calls fence.recover_expired() once to record an observation, sleeps 0.06 s with anyio, and calls it again expecting state 'unknown'. DurableJobRepository.claim_expired (benchbox/mcp/jobs.py:639) treats a lease as expired only when mono_time() has advanced by at least lease_seconds since that first observation. A 10 ms margin sits inside the coarse timer granularity of the Windows runner, so the second call can run too early and the job still reads 'running'. The cause is likely, not proven. Replace the single sleep with a loop that keeps the first recover_expired call (it records the observation), then calls recover_expired every 10 ms until the job is 'unknown' or a 5 s deadline measured with benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time passes, failing with the last observed state. Do not use a fixed count of short sleeps as the bound. Removing the Windows quarantine is handled by nightly-windows-unquarantine-20261008, after a dispatched run on develop shows this leg passing.
